text:
rachel: spotting a steady p99 bump in dedicated-usw1 since ~04:22, small-token chat workloads. looks correlated with TOR packet drops and NIC tx-queue stalls. anyone else seeing this pattern?
owen: yep, dashboards show tor_tx_errors rising in racks r8-r9. can you paste the quick counters?
rachel: logs: 
```
2026-06-09T04:21:56Z tor-agent[tor-9]: tx_drops iface=tor-eth2 delta=780 packets
2026-06-09T04:22:01Z net-proxy[proxy-4]: egress_bytes tenant=tn-300 delta=110MB/s burst=true
2026-06-09T04:22:03Z scheduler[sch]: slab-frag tenant=tn-301 reason=hotspot
```
liu: tn-300 is doing a long-running analytics export; tn-301 just got a fractional promo yesterday and kicked off cross-rack prefill jobs. the combo seems to be filling NIC rings and causing stalls that propagate as p99 latency.
marcos: costs team already pinged me: there's a surprise egress anomaly for org-88. ops wants a short-term throttle.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall. short mitigation plan: 1) apply per-tenant egress leash for the affected pool to 45MB/s, 2) mark new fractional promos as "no-crossrack" for 30m while we investigate, 3) reduce scheduler cross-rack parallelism to 1. can someone run commands?
ops-automation: ready: 
```bash
# leash per-tenant egress for pool
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_per_tenant=true
rctl config set prod pool-proxy egress_leash_bytes_per_sec=47185920
# quarantine new promos
rctl tenant update tn-301 --policy=no-crossrack --note="temp isolation"
# lower parallelism
rctl config set prod allocator prefill_concurrency_limit=1
```
owen: before we flip, quick verification query: 
```sql
SELECT tenant, sum(egress_bytes) as egress FROM net.tor_stats WHERE time > now() - 10m GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY egress DESC LIMIT 5;
```
owen: ran it 3: tn-300 and tn-301 are top two. tn-301 shows many short-lived prefill connections across racks.
rachel: ok apply the leash and quarantine. tagging infra owners.
infra-bot: config change queued user=oncall-sre action=set pool-proxy.egress_leash_per_tenant=true at=2026-06-09T04:24:12Z
ops-automation: applied. egress leash=45MB/s; prefill_concurrency=1; tn-301 policy=no-crossrack.
oncall-sre: monitoring now. please watch p99 and tor tx errors.
liu: within 90s p99 fell from 310ms to ~130ms. tor tx_drops dropped ~70%. egress for tn-301 down to ~6MB/s.
marcos: ops flagged provisional egress charge for org-88 (~0.9TB). we'll hold billing until post-incident write-up.
owen: root cause hypothesis: scheduler allowed concurrent cross-rack warms for a tenant while another tenant was performing heavy egress; NIC queue head-of-line blocking + TOR interface drops caused slab fragmentation and latency spikes. fractional promotions didn't run a headroom check.
rachel: follow-ups: 1) add a scheduler pre-check that queries TOR link headroom and NIC queue depth before kicking off multi-rack warms, 2) make promo flow set default no-crossrack for fractional promos unless explicit opt-in, 3) add alert for sustained per-tenant egress > 60MB/s over 5m in dedicated pools.
liu: also propose a lightweight scheduler probe: attempt a 200ms UDP probe to TOR and measure immediate tx queue free space before allowing cross-rack prefill; cheap and should catch saturated links. i'll sketch a design doc.
oncall-sre: ops asks we also add an automated soft-rollback for promotions that cause immediate egress surge > threshold within 10m.
marcos: will coordinate with billing. please include cost guardrail in the promo checklist.
rachel: i'm filing tickets: scheduler headroom probe, promo-flow defaults, per-tenant egress alert, and promo rollback automation. assigning owners.
owen: thanks all. leaving monitoring on for 20m. ping here if it recurs. :thumbsup:
